anchors: wait for every agent you dispatch before you end your turn
decision: A brief that lets an agent dispatch agents of its own tells it to wait for every agent it dispatches before ending its turn; a report that reaches the dispatcher instead is forwarded to that agent by name with SendMessage.

evidence.text: Queued lesson: four RED/GREEN probes of a background subagent reported into the main session, about 50 failed hand-back attempts were logged, and each report had to be forwarded by SendMessage. Text-only RED probe on the pre-edit text answered NONE.

reopen_if: The harness starts delivering a nested agent's hand-back to its parent after the parent's turn ends, or wakes the parent on it.
why: An agent whose turn ends while its own dispatches run is no longer running to them, so their hand-back fails and each report lands in the main session or is retried until the probe gives up.

anchors: A brief built from an earlier one is re-read whole before dispatch
decision: A brief built by copying an earlier one and replacing some paragraphs is re-read whole before dispatch, and a kept rule that contradicts the new text is dropped or reworded in the same edit.

evidence.text: Quote-back: the pre-edit text answered NONE; opus and haiku arms on the edited text quoted the new paragraph.

reopen_if: Briefs are generated from a single source per dispatch rather than by editing earlier briefs.
why: An agent given a new focus that grants something and a kept rule that forbids it follows the rule, so the granted resource goes unused and the work that needed it is not done.

anchors: Waiting does not save an agent dispatched with `name`
Do not re-dispatch the probe for it.
decision: An agent dispatched with name gets every dispatch's hand-back refused even while it waits; the report is the message input of the probe's last SubagentHandback call in <session>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl, read there (or from the withheld-report-nudge quote), never re-dispatched or re-asked by SendMessage.

evidence.text: Corpus replay of SubagentHandback results by dispatcher (Claude Code 2.1.329): first hand-back refused for 116 of 116 agents a named agent dispatched (all foreground), 0 of 4,319 dispatched by the main session or an unnamed subagent. Pre-edit text probe (opus, haiku): Q1 why and Q3 re-dispatch both NONE. Edited text: both tiers quote the new lines for all three questions.

reopen_if: Claude Code delivers a named agent's dispatches' hand-backs (a replay shows first=OK for named dispatchers), or a background dispatch by a named agent is measured.
why: The waiting rule does not prevent this failure: it is tied to a named dispatcher, not to a turn that ended, so a reader told only to wait re-dispatches or acts without the answer.

decision: A PreToolUse nudge on an Agent dispatch whose prompt mentions probes or meta-skill-writer but lacks a 'wait for every agent you dispatch' line, and a description change to route such dispatches to this skill.

evidence.text: guard_replay over the transcript corpus, tool Agent, field prompt: 341 fires in 5,032 dispatches (723 duplicate records skipped); hand-back failures split by dispatcher kind: 116/116 named, 0/4,319 other.

reopen_if: A hand-back failure is measured from an unnamed dispatcher that ended its turn without waiting.
why: The failure the queue entry reported is not prevented by waiting: every measured failure came from a named dispatcher that was waiting. The nudge would fire on 341 of 5,032 Agent dispatches (6.8%) and stop none of them; the PostToolUse withheld-report-nudge recovers the report instead.

anchors: **A final report in parts, for a background agent.**
decision: A background agent's brief tells it to send its final report with SendMessage in parts of at most about 4,000 characters, changes and evidence first, then tests, decisions, false premises and open items.

evidence.text: 2026-11-20 six-fixer fan-out: 4 of 6 final reports truncated (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: The harness delivers a background agent's whole final report without truncation.
why: The idle notification's result field cuts a long final report off at the end, where the open items and false premises sit.

anchors: **A far-ahead version for a throwaway commit, when the repo's commit gate wants a bump against
decision: When the repo's commit gate wants a bump above origin, a fixer's throwaway commit bumps far above origin (X.99.0), never the next patch; the integrator bumps once at release.

evidence.text: 2026-11-20 seven-fixer fan-out (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: The commit gate stops comparing a commit's version with origin's.
why: Other sessions released twice during one fan-out, and next-patch bumps then sat at or below origin, so the gate refused four fixers' commits.
